title: Human-Centered Swarm Intelligence: Towards a Confucian Ideal of Great Harmony
content: To achieve his ideal of the Great Harmony (Datong), Confucius envisioned a society founded on the altruistic principle that “The world belongs to all”. Yet, inherent human self-interest has long rendered this vision utopian. The rise of the decentralized market economy in modern times has reframed the objective of resource allocation toward guiding self-interested individuals to achieve Pareto optimality—a state that resonates deeply with Confucius’ injunction: “Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire.” Although the conditions for a fully functional decentralized market are highly demanding, advances in information technology and artificial intelligence are increasingly enabling us to approach them, thereby revitalizing the feasibility of a Datong society. However, a critical caveat remains: if general artificial intelligence evolves to serve only a minority rather than all equally, society could be driven in a direction diametrically opposed to the ideal of Great Harmony.
